profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Abnormal AI
profile.summary:
I’m a senior software engineer and tech lead focused on distributed systems, streaming infrastructure, and latency-sensitive production systems.

At Abnormal AI, I build and lead systems operating at the boundary of distributed infrastructure and ML inference, including real-time streaming pipelines, high-QPS backend services, observability platforms, and customer-critical workflows where reliability and tail latency matter.

My work has included reducing database query p99 from ~5s to <50ms at ~500 QPS, redesigning processing architecture to reduce p99 time-to-action from 1.8 hours to 11.44 seconds, and building multi-tenant infrastructure supporting enterprise production workloads.

I’m especially interested in distributed systems, AI infrastructure, model-serving-adjacent systems, streaming platforms, data infrastructure, and building production systems that are scalable and reliable.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
▪ Tech lead for customer-critical distributed systems and real-time security infrastructure, with a focus on reliability, latency, scalability, and production systems operating adjacent to ML inference.

▪ Built low-latency pipeline infrastructure for synchronous ML inference requests in a $32M+ ARR pre-delivery product line, enabling advanced signal enrichment without blocking core mail flow.

▪ Optimized the PostgreSQL datastore behind a high-QPS audit-log service used to hydrate Tier-1 production systems, introducing an asynchronous read replica and redesigning query/index strategy to reduce database query p99 from ~5s to <50ms at ~500 QPS.

▪ Redesigned a latency-sensitive security workflow around dedicated real-time scoring streams, decoupling processing from shared backlog-prone workers and reducing p99 time-to-action from 1.8 hours to 11.44 seconds.

▪ Led a multi-tenant delivery infrastructure initiative supporting 16 enterprise tenants and ~$1.9M ARR, designing automated provisioning for per-tenant TLS certificates and DNS records with zero production operational issues.

▪ Identified and fixed a long-standing correctness issue affecting 34% of mailboxes in a major product stream, preserving a core product guarantee as adoption expanded to larger enterprise deployments.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
▪ Led architecture, design, and rollout of new streaming pipelines for ML-backed decisioning on a Google Workspace-specific product line, delivering 2 weeks ahead of schedule to fill a critical protection gap for ~$5M in protected ARR.


▪ Architected a multi-region remediation and mail-ingestion path with failover mechanisms that preserved message delivery and minimized downtime in customer-critical email workflows.

▪ Built and operated real-time distributed ingestion and streaming systems upstream of ML detection pipelines, ensuring reliable message intake and low-latency handoff for systems dependent on model inference.

▪ Architected and implemented a Firehose → S3 → Databricks observability pipeline for a P0 remediation system, enabling per-message investigations and deterministic lookups for the first time and establishing a reusable pattern later adopted by other teams.

▪ Pioneered AI-enabled engineering workflows for my team by creating agent-friendly service context, documentation, and validation workflows that increased development velocity and enabled safer, higher-confidence AI-assisted changes across services and dashboards.

▪ Built self-serve tooling, alerting, and operational context that reduced investigation toil and eased on-call burden, including an internal tool that eliminated ~75% of CS/Product inquiries while improving team autonomy.

▪ Led performance and scalability improvements across large-scale search infrastructure, including an OpenSearch sharding and partitioning initiative that reduced latency of customer-facing queries by 75%+ across hundreds of millions of documents.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
▪ Drove the design, development, and operation of distributed cloud-based systems using Go, MySQL, and message queues, delivering scalable, fault-tolerant, and highly reliable solutions.
▪ Acted as a key liaison for product and engineering stakeholders from multiple teams to drive projects from conception to completion.
▪Implemented platform-wide database sharding in a multi-tenant cloud environment, enabling a seamless transition for all back-end development teams to horizontal scalability of MySQL databases.
▪Led the strategic migration of single-tenant databases (billions of rows, terabytes of data) from an on-premise monolith to a multitenant cloud environment on Amazon RDS.
▪ Spearheaded documentation best practices, instilling a robust culture of documentation within the team.
▪ Provided comprehensive code reviews, elevating the skills of peers and ensuring top-tier code quality across multiple repositories.
▪ Introduced real-time dashboarding and monitoring systems, ensuring swift team response to production issues.
▪ Created and maintained essential platform tools, accelerating local development processes for the entire team.
▪ Proficiently navigated a 'backend for frontends' pattern to deliver optimized backend solutions.
▪ Optimized and maintained essential developer tools, accelerating local development processes for the entire team.
▪ Introduced real-time dashboarding and monitoring systems, ensuring swift team response to production issues.
▪Achieved FedRAMP compliance for the Value Team’s microservices
and external enterprise data warehouse (EDW) solution .
positions.insights: Skills: Go · MySQL · Redis · Docker · Unit Testing · Git · Integration Testing · Database Design · GitHub · RabbitMQ · Relational Databases

projects.title: INTEX
projects.description:
For the last week of classes in the Fall 2020 semester, BYU's Information Systems program had an integrated exercise (INTEX). The project lasted 5 days and we each spent about 48-60 hours working on the project.

 In INTEX, we were each placed in a group of four, and in that group we were asked to create a website connected to a database that would recommend employers to job applicants, and job applicants to employers. The recommendations were based on job applicants that those employers had already hired.

We split up the workload among the four of us, and I was in charge of creating the recommender. The recommender portion was one of the most difficult and frustrating things I have ever done, but by putting in hard work, searching online forums, and collaborating with my group members, I was able to figure it out and finish it on time.
